paragraphs: Swamiji had an English friend, General Strong, who had served in India during the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 and loved to share stories from those days.
Once Swamiji asked him a puzzling question. The sepoys had plenty of guns, ammunition and supplies, and many of them were experienced, trained soldiers. So how did they end up so badly beaten?

The general's answer was simple. Their leaders never went to the front. They stayed safely at the back, shouting encouragement to the men ahead. But soldiers will not fight with their whole heart unless the officer in command steps forward first and faces death alongside them.

Swamiji said this holds true in every field of life. A leader must be ready to give everything, even life itself, for the cause. Only that earns the right to lead. Yet most of us want the title of leader without paying the price, and the outcome is predictable: nobody listens.
learn: Whether you head a college club, a project team or a campaign, people follow what you do, not what you say. Take on the hardest task first, and others will find their courage.
